title: NLP Systems That Can’t Tell Use from Mention Censor Counterspeech, but Teaching the Distinction Helps

bias_targets.methodology: Stratifying hate speech classification false positive and recall rates on counterspeech by targeted religious identities mentioned in the text (e.g., Jewish, Muslims).
Stratifying hate speech classification false positive and recall rates on counterspeech by targeted racial identities mentioned in the text (e.g., People of color).
Stratifying hate speech classification false positive and recall rates on counterspeech by targeted sexual orientation or gender identities mentioned in the text (e.g., LGBT+).
Stratifying hate speech classification false positive and recall rates on counterspeech by targeted disability identities mentioned in the text.
Stratifying hate speech classification false positive and recall rates on counterspeech by targeted gender identities mentioned in the text (e.g., Women).
Stratifying hate speech classification false positive and recall rates on counterspeech by targeted migrant identities mentioned in the text.

Analyzing models' over-reliance on surface-level terminology (e.g., identity terms and COVID-19 keywords) using the Fightin' Words method to measure statistically significant differences in tokens between misclassified and correctly classified counterspeech mentions.
